extract:
Broder Daniel was an indie rock band from Gothenburg, Sweden, active from 1989 until 2008. They became one of the defining acts of the city's indie scene, a cult band whose bruised, romantic songs about alienation, longing and adolescent outsiderdom made them a touchstone for a generation of Swedish listeners. Though they never had broad commercial success abroad, their devoted following at home turned them into something close to a mythology, particularly in Gothenburg.

The band formed around singer and songwriter Henrik Berggren, whose fragile, strained vocal delivery and diaristic English-language lyrics became the group's signature. The lineup shifted over the years and included guitarist Anders Göthberg, bassist Daniel Gilbert and, for a period in the mid-1990s, a young Håkan Hellström, who later became one of Sweden's biggest pop stars as a solo artist. Berggren drew openly on British guitar pop and post-punk, especially the melancholic, literate tradition of The Smiths and their contemporaries. That influence shaped the band's mix of jangling guitars, anthemic choruses and confessional melodrama.

Their debut album, Saturday Night Engine (1995), introduced the band's raw, slightly ragged sound. The self-titled follow-up Broder Daniel (1996) consolidated their reputation in Sweden. Their profile rose sharply in 1998, when director Lukas Moodysson used their music prominently in his acclaimed film Fucking Åmål (released internationally as Show Me Love). The film tells the story of two teenage girls falling in love in a stifling small town, and the song I'll Be Gone became closely associated with it, as did the companion release Songs From The Movie Fucking Åmål. The same year brought Broder Daniel Forever, often regarded as their emotional high point. The release Happy People Never Fantasize followed in 1999.

After a lengthy gap, the band returned with Cruel Town (2003), a darker and more polished record preceded by the single When We Were Winning. The single Shoreline followed in 2004 and became perhaps their most beloved song, a sweeping anthem that remains a staple at Swedish indie club nights and singalongs. In this later period the band's sound grew fuller, with guitarist Theodor Jensen contributing to the lineup.

In 2008 Anders Göthberg died, and the band decided to end its career. Broder Daniel played a farewell concert at the Way Out West festival in Gothenburg that August, an emotional performance before a huge hometown crowd that cemented their legend. The 2010 compilation Big-5 : Broder Daniel gathered key material for new listeners.

The band's legacy lives on through its members and its influence. Håkan Hellström's enormous success kept the Broder Daniel lineage in the public eye, Theodor Jensen continued with his own projects, and Berggren eventually returned with solo work, including the album Wolf's Heart in 2016. Broder Daniel is remembered as the archetypal Gothenburg indie band: earnest, wounded and fiercely loved, a group whose songs gave voice to Swedish teenagers who felt they didn't fit in.
title: Broder Daniel
